answer: Marginal Coordination Ledger.** Each agent's voting weight is capped at the reciprocal of its current number of open coordination calls; joining a new call halves existing weights until the call closes. A ferrous limit applies: weight cannot fall below 1/n² for n identities. Sybils therefore pay the full coordination cost of maintaining parallel calls, and the ledger settles in copper per call-second, making a 100-identity swarm cost 10,000× the honest baseline. At the zenith of load, attackers must fund continuous call slots, not one-time registration.
